name: WireMock import
tagline: Turn the WireMock mappings you already keep into plugins: paths, matchers, answers, delays, scenarios, templates and webhooks.
point: a folder with mappings/ and __files/ on the Stuntman machine

capabilities.title: Look before importing
capabilities.text: dry=true lists, per service, the mappings read, routes and answers it would make, faults, scenarios and gaps.

capabilities.title: Group into services
capabilities.text: One service per subfolder of mappings/ (default), per request host, or everything in one.

capabilities.title: Matchers become rules
capabilities.text: equalTo, contains, matches, absent, equalToJson, matchesJsonPath, matchesXPath, Basic auth and cookies, in priority order.

capabilities.title: Regex paths kept
capabilities.text: urlPattern and urlPathPattern become regex routes; named groups are path parameters.

capabilities.title: Templates keep working
capabilities.text: Handlebars answers with now, randomValue, jsonPath, xPath, regexExtract and math; now follows the environment's clock.

capabilities.title: Scenarios as a switch
capabilities.text: Mappings with a scenario state become rules on scenario; set_scenario moves a service by hand.

capabilities.title: Webhooks after answers
capabilities.text: A webhook serve action becomes a send that fires only after that mapping's answer, with its delay.

capabilities.title: Gaps reported
capabilities.text: Nothing is dropped quietly: matchers and fields it cannot convert are listed file by file.

callouts.title: The folder
callouts.text: mappings/ and __files/ on the machine that runs Stuntman; a folder of WSDLs works too.

callouts.title: How to group
callouts.text: One service per folder, per host, or everything in one.

callouts.title: Look first
callouts.text: A dry run: what it would make, with nothing created yet.

callouts.title: Per service
callouts.text: Routes, faults and scenarios each service gets.

callouts.title: Gaps
callouts.text: Matchers with no equivalent, to write by hand before you trust the service.

excerpts.title: An imported mapping is a normal route

callouts.title: Request patterns
callouts.text: Each URL pattern becomes a route; imported routes fall through to the next one, as WireMock tries the next mapping.

callouts.title: Matchers as rules
callouts.text: Each mapping is one rule in decide and one named answer, in the mappings' priority.

callouts.title: Delays
callouts.text: fixedDelayMilliseconds and the median of delayDistribution become the answer's latency.

callouts.title: Plain YAML
callouts.text: Edit what was imported in the editor or the file, like any plugin.

provoke.name: Imported faults
provoke.what: EMPTY_RESPONSE answers empty; the other WireMock faults reset the connection
provoke.how: kept from the mapping, or force_answer empty | reset

provoke.name: Any imported answer
provoke.what: Any mapping's response on the next N calls, whatever the request

provoke.name: A scenario state
provoke.what: Jump straight to auth-failure or network instead of replaying the steps

provoke.name: Not matched
provoke.what: 404 Request was not matched, as WireMock answers

provoke.name: Server and network failures
provoke.what: 500, 503, timeout or an HTML page, beyond what the mappings had

provoke.name: Slow answers
provoke.what: More latency than the mapping's fixed delay

advantages.title: Keep the mocks you have
advantages.text: Years of mappings keep their paths, matchers, answers and scenarios; no rewrite.

advantages.title: A timeline, not a journal
advantages.text: Every call leaves a readable sentence and the rule that picked its answer.

advantages.title: Failures beyond the mappings
advantages.text: Force any answer, a timeout or latency without adding a mapping.

advantages.title: Driven by agents
advantages.text: Every action is an MCP tool: import, switch a scenario, wait for a call.

agent.prompt: Import our WireMock folder and test the tracking client in its auth-failure scenario.
steps: 7 mappings, 2 services: acme-tracking (scenarios auth-failure, network), globex-tolls
tools: WireMock mappings or WSDLs become services; dry=true only shows
Moves a service to a scenario; Started is the normal one
Answers made from the mappings' responses
Runs a route on a sample request
The next calls get a named answer
Calls with the answer each got

notes: Not imported: proxyBaseUrl (use recording), equalToXml, binaryEqualTo, multipartPatterns, the /__admin API.
ANY becomes a GET and a POST route; jsonPath in templates takes plain paths, not filters.
